Please find enclosed the three separate Official Notes that we compiled regarding these interviews." Is this note that you were sent the interview records of Veselin Karanovic and Marija Djuric? If I could take you to paragraph 17 of your supplementary statement, Mr. Zganjer, you say -- you identified that document, and you said: "This was received by me together with the enclose issues in the document." This is the document, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO ZGANJER
utterances.text: I confirm that this document was, indeed, given to me and that I received it with all of these enclosures. I received it personally, because if you look at the stamp in the upper right corner, that's where I inscribed in my own hand the name of the case file that was given to this case at the state attorney's office.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, may I move this document into evidence, please, and this is again included in the bar table submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And it is not subject, as such, to the objections from what I understand. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit number P1053.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P1053 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, can I have document P622, please, P622.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, while that document is brought up on the screen, Mr. Zganjer, if I could take you to paragraph 24 of your supplementary statement, you say: "I'm now shown a copy of the work plan drafted by Ivica Vesel, and approved by Gojko Markovic, chief of general crime department, dated 13th November, 2001, referred to above. This is a plan to conduct an investigation into the deaths in Grubori in August 1995." In the next line, you say: "This document was received by me and I have seen it before. It was sent to me enclosed with a letter of 14 December 2001 from chief of crime police department." Then about two lines down, you say: "In the course of the investigation, the criminal police have gathered documentation referred to under the heading numbered 2, documentation. One of the documents collected from the special police administration and referred to in this document is the response to the letter of Elisabeth Rehn, composed on 30 March 1996 by the special police sector and signed by the by the special advisor to the minister, Mladen Markac. Special police and crime police are both part of MUP, and, as such, these documents were collected by the crime police through official means."

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, if we could move, Mr. Registrar, to page 6 of the English translation and page 3 of the Croatian version.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: There in the documentation, the first paragraph reads: "The special police administration provided the documentation compiled with respect to the implementation of Obruc police operation within the military police Operation Storm; namely, the following ..."

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And if could you move, Mr. Registrar, to the next page on both versions.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: There, just under that letter of Elisabeth Rehn, it reads in the English version: "Official statement in reply," and, in fact, you corrected that translation in proofing, where you said, "response to the letter of Elisabeth Rehn, composed on 13 March 1996 by the special police sector, and signed by the special advisor to the minister, Mladen Markac." And, Mr. Zganjer, I showed this document to you because it is relevant to the next document, and I will ask you the question. It is it already in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: But while we're still on this document, if you could move -- Mr. Registrar, if I can now call up document number 493.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: While that's coming up, I want to refer you to your statement again, Mr. Zganjer. In paragraph 25 of your supplementary statement, you read -- you say: "I'm now shown a copy of a report from the chief of Sibenik-Knin crime police department, addressed to the Sibenik county prosecutor, dated 8 February 2002. The report attaches documentation gathered during the investigation into the killings in Grubori. I received this report and the enclosed files referred to." Now, is this the document that you're referring to at paragraph 25?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO ZGANJER
utterances.text: Yes, that's the document. I received it, and it bears the date 8 February 2002. If the registrar, please, lowers down the document, you will see in the right upper corner that I inscribed the markings of the file in my own handwriting. This is the number under which this case was filed in my office in Sibenik, and the number is K or D044/01, in my own handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... on page 1, if could I read the heading, you say -- they refer to your communication, that is Mr. Zganjer, your communication. Reference numbers are given, and the first paragraph reads: "Through further action, following your request, we have taken operative and criminal investigation measures and accordingly gathered additional documents. The following documents are enclosed ..."

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And if we could move, Mr. Registrar, to page 2 of the English version as well as the B/C/S, the Croatian version.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Under the heading contained in file number 3, it reads: "Special police sector documents." The second document enclosed is -- it reads in the English translation: "Disclosure of information, "and you again corrected that during the proofing to be an incorrect translation, and you said "response regarding Elisabeth Rehn's letter, compiled on 13 March 1996 by the special police sector, and signed by the special advisor to the minister, Mladen Markac." That document has been enclosed and sent to you with this letter. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO ZGANJER
utterances.text: When it comes to the letter written by Elisabeth Rehn and opinion on it compiled by the special police sector, it is signed by the special advisor to the minister, Mladen Markac. This opinion can also be found enclosed to the documents that were submitted to me. However, correct me if I'm wrong, I believe that this opinion did not get to me with Mladen Markac s signature. It arrived without that signature. But I would like to see the document that is on the files of the state attorney's office, and then I will be able to see whether I'm right or not. I believe that the opinion that I received did not contain Mr. Markac's signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I will show that you document, Mr. Zganjer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne, you will do that now, because I'm seeking a time for a break. If you would first like to --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Tender this, yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objection. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, this becomes Exhibit number P1054.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P1054 is admitted into evidence. If you want to deal with the signature issue right away, Ms. Mahindaratne, that might be the logical thing to do before the break.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, actually, there are two other issues with regard to this document. I wanted to deal quickly with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But then, I think, since many of you have been waiting here on from 10.30 already in this courtroom, then I'd first have a break. Mr. Zganjer, keep this document well in your mind because further documents will be put to you after the break. We will have a break and we will resume at a quarter to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Zganjer, I'd like to just go back to the document on the screen; and below that document we just referred to, there is again -- this is at the bottom of the English translation and halfway through in the Croatian version. It says: "Contained in file number 3," and you think that is probably a mistake. You think it should read file 4. And in file 4, you sent 17 Official Notes of interviews conducted with Lucko anti-terrorist members. Then under file number 5?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: If we could on the English translation move, Mr. Registrar, to the next page, and remain on the same page on the Croatian version.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Under file number 5, you're sent material regarding the check -- regarding the vehicles observed at the incident seen in Plavno village, 25 August 1995, and three Official Notes on interviews with -- which the official record of interview with Ivan Cermak." Now, you wish to see particularly the document we referred to before the break.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if I could call document P505, at MFI state, at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: While that is being brought up, Mr. Zganjer, if I could ask you to look at your supplemental statement. At paragraph 26, you say: "I'm now shown a copy of a letter from Mladen Markac addressed to the minister of the interior, Ivan Jarnjak, in response to a letter from Elisabeth Rehn." The report is dated 13 March 1996 and you give a reference number, which is the reference number on the document on your screen. "This is a letter referred to about a document bearing 03500258 to 0259, as well as in the work plan, bearing number 03500519 to 0523. This would be the letter I received. I believe I received a copy of the original document which was sent to Minister Jarnjak. I'm now shown a copy of this document without a signature. I believe the copy which was sent to me did not have a signature. It is likely that the original letter received by Jarnjak had a signature. I did not have any reason to doubt the authenticity of the document since I received it from the crime police through official channels." Now, Mr. Zganjer, is this the document - I'm referring to the document on the screen - is this the document you're referring to in paragraph 26 of your supplementary statement? And if you want to go into the next page, please let me know.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO ZGANJER
utterances.text: Will you please show me the next page, next page. Yes, that's the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zganjer.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, this document is currently in an MFI state on the basis that the Defence had objected. I believe I established the basis for admission.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I believe not, Your Honour. There is no basis at all. The document is still unstamped, unsigned, and has no official number in the head of the documents. So the Defence very much doubts whether this is an authentic document, no matter which was the sources that the witness has been obtained with this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the witness has testified, and in his words, he says, "I did not have any reason to doubt the authenticity of the document since I received it from the crime police through official channels." Now, if the suggestion of the Defence is that there has been some fabrication within the official channels, then it is up to the Defence to tender that in evidence. I believe we have established a foundation on the basis for admission of the document. There is a witness who identifies the document and who says that he has received it in the course of the investigation initiated by him. He has received it through official channels and he says he has no reason to doubt the authenticity. We are referring to here the state prosecutor who has received documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Well, as we are speaking on the subject, I will ask my learned friend from the Prosecutor's bench to ask the witness of the certain lack of signature stamp and the official number of the documents; and, afterwards, my learned friend could ask the witness whether this is an example of the usual official documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. I think existence of stamps and signatures, we don't have to put many questions to the witness in relation to that, I would say. Yes, although it would have been a matter -- of course, it is triggered more or less by the discussion on admissibility of this document, Ms. Mahindaratne, where I would otherwise would have expected Mr. Mikulicic to deal with the matter in cross-examination. Yes, I'm not blaming you, Mr. Mikulicic, let that be clear. But, of course, I'm thinking aloud about where --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, while you are thinking aloud, I would also say something in that manner. I would like to think aloud. The Prosecution had Elisabeth Rehn on the stand as a witness. Why did they ask her if he ever received this document. That would the proper way to establish the foundation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: -- not through the witness who is not issuing the documents --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mikulicic, we are -- Mr. Mikulicic --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Okay, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- we're not going to argue the matter in the presence of the witness. Let me just check. Yes, Mr. Zganjer, could I ask you the following question: If you were copied on a letter sent to, as in this case, Mr. Jarnjak, was it common, uncommon, did it happen oft, did it happen sometimes, that the copy you received would be an unsigned one, an unstamped one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was standard procedure for anyone sending a document to me to stamp it and sign it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But that was not my question, as you may be aware. It was about when you were copied on a document, in this case a letter sent to another person. So if you were sent a copy of that letter, whether it would always be signed and stamped.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document was sent to me, and I said the following about the document in my statement: I believe this to be an authentic document. Now, why did I say that? It wasn't the veterinarian service that sent me this document. I got it from the Sibenik-Knin police administration, which was an integral part of the Ministry of Interior. That is the key to my belief that the document is an authentic one because of its source and because of the person who produced this document, regardless of the fact that the person did not actually sign the document. To me, it was Mr. Mladen Markac who produced this letter. However, was this letter eventually forwarded to the minister of the interior, Ivan Jarnjak, or not? Was it stamped and signed by Mladen Markac for that person? I don't know. But here you have my reasons for believing that this is an authentic document. It's about disclosure. And in terms of substance, this is a response to the letter that Ms. Elisabeth Rehn had previously sent to the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. One additional question: Do you remember any incident ever that you would receive a copy of a document, which was not addressed to you but just copied to you, from this same source, that is, the Sibenik-Knin police administration, where the copy that was September to you was not the same as what was sent to the person to whom the letter was addressed? Did you ever experience that something went wrong there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Regrettably, I cannot answer this specifically, Your Honours. I simply don't remember. Nevertheless, it is a normal course of action even for Official Notes that I was receiving to be signed by whoever produced them and to be stamped by the relevant police administration on its way out. Despite all of this, some of the Official Notes were neither signed nor stamped. Again, as I was receiving all these documents from the Sibenik-Knin police administration, who, in turn, had probably got them from the crime police police administration which was part of the Ministry of Interior, at the time, I had no reason to question the authenticity of these documents, despite certain formal shortcomings that they may have manifested.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Mahindaratne. The Chamber will decide on the admission of this document. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. Registrar, may I call document number 4388, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: This is the document that you decided is actually not admissible in evidence. This is the interview of Mr. Cermak --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. President. That was my mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I withdraw that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Zganjer, now, do you recall that memo that was sent to you by the chief of crime police department on 8th February 2002, that we just looked at a little while ago, where we looked at the files, and I'm referring to P1054. You noted that you were also sent 17 official records of interview with members of the Lucko Unit. Now, in fact, if I could take to you paragraph 30 of your supplementary statement, Mr. Zganjer, you state the following: "I was also sent a number of Official Notes of interviews with members of Lucko Unit or the special police, and I'm now shown these documents and I can confirm that I received these documents from the Sibenik-Knin crime police. I believe that the marking on the documents, some of the text being underlined, were made by me." Then you identify and authenticate six Official Notes of interviews.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, there has been no specific objection in relation to the admission of these six documents, with the exception of the general, the blanket objection from the Gotovina Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: That's not true.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I'm sorry. With regard to Mr. Balunovic, I beg your pardon, I will call the documents in, Mr. President. Mr. Registrar, can I have document number 2653, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, while that is being brought up, Mr. Zganjer, if I could take you to the first document you authenticated. You referred to the Official Notes of interview with Ivica Matanic compiled on 4 December 2001 in Zagreb police administration. Is this the note you referred to and you recognise the markings on the document?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO ZGANJER
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could both of witness's microphones be switched on please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see page 1 of the notes, but I believe there might be another page.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... could we move to page 2.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. This is the Official Note that was delivered to me, and there was an attachment which is the document that we spoke about a while ago. The underlining is, well, it's just like that. It is a personal feature of my work. I use this to mark out certain portions of the statement that I for various reasons might find to be of particular interest.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I move to tender this into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I object this, Your Honour, on the very same reason that we were talking about the Official Notes as an evidence on the beginning of today's session and when you brought up the decision that your final decision you will postpone until the results of the proceedings. It could be marked as MFI but not as an evidence. That is my position because we cannot --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that it is tendered into evidence, and what you expect the Chamber in line with its earlier guidance would do is to invite Mr. Registrar to mark it for identification, which is what I have done by now.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit number P1055, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P1055 is marked for identification. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, there is five other notes, and I understand there is an objection. May I just tender it from the bar table, and I understand they will be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And those that will remain on the list you will provide to Mr. Registrar, so that he can assign MFI numbers for those documents as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, may I have document number --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we do so, apart from that we have dealt with the issue of whether this type of material is admissible into evidence, is there any objection against trying to introduce it through the bar table, rather than to put it to the witness. Is there any issue? I'm just --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I could only predict that the answer of the witness will be exactly the same as it relates to the first one, so I don't think it is worth time consuming to go through whole procedure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is understood. I want to avoid that we have later overlooked some issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: No, I think Mr. Mikulicic has said it perfectly clearly. The objection stands. But if it's through the bar table, it makes no difference to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. Registrar, may I call for document D738, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: While the document is brought up, Mr. Zganjer, if you could look at paragraph 31 of your supplementary statement. You say: "I'm now shown a report from chief of Sibenik-Knin crime police department addressed to county prosecutor Sibenik, dated 14th December 2001. The report attaches notes of interviews carried out as part of the investigation into the killings in Grubori." Is this a document you identified by paragraph 31?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO ZGANJER
utterances.text: I must raise a matter at this point. I believe you've now read out parts of paragraphs 31 and 33. Now which specific paragraph do you have in mind by your question?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Zganjer. I think you perhaps -- you didn't hear me. I was reading paragraph 31. Let me read it again: "I'm now shown a report from the chief of Sibenik-Knin crime police department, addressed to county prosecutor Sibenik, dated 14th December 2001. The report attached notes of interviews carried out as part of the investigation into the killings in Grubori." I'm asking you if this is the document you referred to in paragraph 31?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO ZGANJER
utterances.text: Yes, that's the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I move this into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Any objections? No objections. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe this already in evidence as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. President. It is already in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is already in evidence. Now, Ms. Mahindaratne, the only question you put in relation to this document to the witness is whether this was the document. The documents that an ERN number. It's specified in his statement. Is there any need to assume that what shown to him, as far as ERN numbers is concerned, that there are any mistakes there, because otherwise -- or would we go through all of the documents? Of course, there could be mistakes. Since also the subject, especially in paragraph 31, even the subject is mentioned, ERN number is given. And I'm also looking at the Defence. Is there any need to verify for all of these documents whether this is the document shown to the witness? If so, we have quite lot of work to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, not from the Gotovina Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I think we would take the same position. If this is just a rehearsal of identifying ERN numbers, I agree, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Mikulicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: We are taking the very same position, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne, therefore, unless there is any reason to have doubts whether there could be confusion as far as documents are concerned, then there is no need to repeat in court what the witness said already in his supplementary statement --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Actually, I had intended to submit all these documents from the bar table, but I particularly brought this document up because it encloses an interview note of Nada Surjak, where the Cermak Defence particularly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you wanted to --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Because of the specific objection in relation to that Official Note, I believe that I want to bring it up in court. That is the only reason.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But you only asked whether this is it the document, and then you gave an ERN number. That is the only thing you did.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President. Then I was going to go to the contents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. If you want to put further questions. I took it, but perhaps I'm wrong, that once you've put it to the witness, and if you are seeking it to be admitted into evidence, that you've then dealt with the document. But I might be wrong in that respect and then my apologies for that. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Can I just before we embark on what my learned friend has just notified the Court that she is going to ask the about the content of the statement, again I don't need to repeat myself. My understanding is that she wants to put questions about the Official Note in respect of that particular individual.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President. I was going try get him to confirm that he had received the note of Nada Surjak.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If I would have remained silent, we might have saved sometime. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Zganjer, by this note, you have been sent four Official Notes of interviews which includes the interview note of Nada Surjak, and I want to take you to that particular note.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if I could call -- have on the screen document number 3298.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could save some time for the court, we are ready to stipulate - I'm talking about the Markac Defence, of course - we are ready to stipulate that all those Official Notes has been received by the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know whether that resolves all of your concern, Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President. In which event, I will move on, but let me just ask one question with regard to this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're free to put any question. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Zganjer, do you note the document on the screen, and you identified earlier on that you -- that certain notations on these documents were made by you. Are these underlinings made by you?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO ZGANJER
utterances.text: I am familiar with the document, and as for the interventions, i.e., the underlining, that is what I did myself. I am the author of these interventions.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court, in terms of underlining, what is exactly -- what is the process you went through in reviewing these documents?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO ZGANJER
utterances.text: Of course, I read these documents; and as I've already told you, there are some things that seemed important and that's why I underlined them. The underlinings would have helped me to focus on the important bits of the text on a second reading. I would call it a rationalisation of time, a time-saving technique.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zganjer.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, may it be marked for identification, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit number P1056, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It will keep that status for the time being.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if I could call document 3476. This is also one of the press articles to which Defence objected, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And, Mr. Zganjer, I appreciate that you may not have seen this document or press article.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: If we could go, Mr. Registrar, to page 3 of the Croatian version and in the English version 03524451. If could you focus on that photograph, and if you could just take -- oh, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: There is an photograph of reporter interviewing Mr. Cermak on this -- in this picture. Can you tell Court who that reporter is based on this article -- let me just make it shorter. Do you agree that it was Ms. Nada Surjak, whom we just referred to, who is seen interviewing Mr. Cermak in Grubori here?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO ZGANJER
utterances.text: I can see Mr. Cermak depicted in the photograph, there is no doubt about that. And as for the lady depicted in the photo, I can just see her profile. I might agree that this is Mrs. Nada Surjak, a journalist of the Croatian Television.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zganjer.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: May this document be given MFI status, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit number P1057, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: May I also, Mr. President, submit from the bar table document number 3297, which is a memo which also attaches an Official Note of interview. And, Mr. Registrar, if I could have 3297. I'm just submitting this from the bar table, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: It has attached to the document official record of interview, Mr. President, so considering the guidelines given, although the cover sheet could be admitted. Since there is an attachment which is a official record of interview, maybe it could be given a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Cover letter, I'm a bit confused Ms. Mahindaratne. I always understand tendering from the bar table to be that without showing it or even presenting it to the witness, that you would seek it to be admitted into evidence; whereas, what you're doing is you're showing it to the witness and then saying you want to tender it from the bar table, although no questions were put to the witness. So it seems to be a kind of intermediate procedure. Mr. Registrar, the cover letter, just the cover letter, would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes Exhibit number P1058.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P1058 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And page 2 and 3 may be given an MFI status, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Second, third page, the attached Official Note, Mr. Registrar, would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P1059, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And it keeps that status for the time being. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: May I have document 6087, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Zganjer, in this document on the screen, the chief of crime police department reports to you on the following lines. He says: "After additional action, following your request, interviews have been conducted with General Mladen Markac and Mr. Zeljko Sacic concerning their knowledge of events in the village of Grubori on 25th August 1995 when a number of people perished." Now, in relation to that, at paragraph 27, referring to your notes --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: This for the record, Mr. President, has been tendered with the bar table motion, bar table submission.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: It says: "At entry 12 of my notes, I have made a note of investigative plans to conduct an interview with the command structure of the special police, Mladen Markac, and Zeljko Sacic, in order to ascertain the type of weapons used at the time of the Grubori incident, as a shell casing was found by the bed of one of the victims. We requested details from the special police of the type of weapons allocated to each officer at the time, and also requested ballistic testing to ascertain whether the shell casing matched a weapon in possession of the special police at the time. I do not believe we received any such details of weapons used by the special police before my tenure in Sibenik ended in September 2002." Now, can you explain to Court what steps did you do when you did not get the required information from the special police sector?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO ZGANJER
utterances.text: There is a conversation that I held with the police officials who were involved in the criminal proceedings in this case. I made a note of that conversation on the cover of my case file. In that conversation, we looked at the possibility that you're talking about at the moment, where I described in my statement under bullet point 27. The photos from the place of the incident in Grubori, as far as can I remember, depicts, or at least one of them depicts, the body of an elderly man next to a bed. As far as I can remember, he was shot in the head. That photo also it depicts a bullet casing. I repeat, this is as much as I can remember after seven or eight years. There was some indicia that the bullet casing found by that body was in the possession of UN members, i.e., one of them who had taken the photo originally. We were then supposed to take steps to see whether we can get a hold of that bullet casing. And since we had already identified that, in the zone of responsibility in the area of Grubori, a special police units was in place at the time of the incident, it only seemed logical that we would try and get hold of the weaponry of that unit and of any written traces as to the fact who of the members carried or had been issued with what weapons. We were supposed to identify the serial number or some other identification marks of that weapon; and then if we were able to get hold of the bullet casing, we were supposed to carry out ballistic expertise, in order to establish whether the bullet had been fired from any of the weapons of that particular unit. The only thing that we were able to find of that bullet was its casing, nothing else. If the ballistic expertise were to prove that, then based on all the documents collected about the persons who had been issued with certain types of weapons, we have been able to arrive at a possible suspect or the perpetrator of the crime, which was the killing of that elderly man who had been shot dead lying by his bed or in his bed. I don't know what happened. I stopped working in Sibenik in 2002. I don't know whether anything was done to this effect. I repeat, on the 15th of September, 2002, I left that position. I am -- I continued working in the state attorney's office but in a different position. However, there is an written trace of my conversation with the police officials about this issue. You can find it on the cover of my case file where I provided a summary of that conversation and my requests towards the police as to what they were supposed to do with this regard.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Zganjer, were you given a further explanation by any authorities as to why these steps had not been carried out during 1995, soon after the incident, or until you instructed these steps to be carried out in 2001?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO ZGANJER
utterances.text: Well, this may not have been exactly the subject of my interest. In my statement that I provided to the investigators of the OTP of this Tribunal, I stated very clearly when I had first learned about this incident in Grubori. I also stated what I did with this regard after my initial information. It arises from what I stated and from the written documents on the case file what my points of interest were and what dilemmas I had to eliminate and what it was I actually wanted to establish.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Zganjer, you may have misunderstood me. It was not a criticism against you. My question was whether you had ever received any information as to why these investigative steps had not been carried out in 1995, soon after the incident when the matter was fresh, why nothing of this sort this been done until you instructed the police to carry out these steps?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO ZGANJER
utterances.text: I've already said, and I repeat, when I learned about the incident in Grubor, I contacted my colleague in Zadar, an official with the state attorney's office there. Why did I contact my colleague in Zadar? I did that because of area of Knin, including the area of the settlement, or, rather, the village of Grubori, was also under the authority of the state attorney's office of Zadar and the court of Zadar. Also, it was within the jurisdiction of the police administration of the county of Zadar and Knin. I asked my colleague in Zadar whether he had ever received a report on the incident in Grubori. He told me that he hadn't. I asked him that either in 1998 or 1999 when the area of Knin, or the general area of Knin, was returned to the county of Sibenik-Knin and when it fell within the jurisdiction of my office of the state attorney, the office that I headed. My colleague in Zadar did not know anything about that at all. I suppose that the investigating judge didn't know anything either. Why this was not investigated from the -- from the moment it happened in 1995 to sometime in 1999 or 2000, when I started investigating the whole matter, I really wouldn't know. You would have to ask somebody else about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Zganjer. Based on this letter that is the document on the screen, it is -- it indicates that it was upon your -- following your instructions that Mr. Mladen Markac and Mr. Zeljko Sacic had been interviewed by the Sibenik-Knin crime police. Now, what were your reasons to instruct the police to interview Mr. Markac and Mr. Sacic?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO ZGANJER
utterances.text: The reasons were very clear and very simple. I learned that special police was active in the area, and I learned which unit of the special police were active. It was only logical for me to ask for Mr. Markac and Sacic to be interviewed because they belonged to the structure of the special police units.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And having interviewed them, did you receive any information or assistance which facilitated your investigation any further from either Mr. Markac or Mr. Sacic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Objections. The witness didn't say that he personally interviewed those --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I understood --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: -- individuals.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I understood this to be once interviews were held with them, because apparently that's what the letter says: "Interviews have been conducted with ..." That's how I understood it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, the question to you was whether you received any information or assistance which facilitated your investigation any further from either Mr. Markac or Mr. Sacic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I can remember, the statements provided by Mr. Markac and Mr. Sacic did not contain any information that would shed light on the whole event. I repeat, I really can't remember the contents of their statements; but, by and large, they spoke of the alleged armed conflict involving the special police of the Republic of Croatia and the remains of the other party to the conflict, the members of the other party to the conflict. I may be mistaken. I am trying to remember. There was a difference there as to whether these people, the elderly people, got in between the exchange of fire between the warring parties, or they were allegedly executed by the members of the enemy army, because they had not agreed to put up resistance to the Croatian armed force. Something along these lines, roughly, was said. That was the position, as it were, that one could discern from the statements of the members of the special police including the statements provided by Messrs. Markac and Sacic, as far as I can remember, as I sit here today.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zganjer.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, may I tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I have no objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit number P1060.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P1060 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And the attached statements, 65 ter 326 and 327, the Official Notes of records, will be tendered from the bar table, Mr. President, later on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will find them then on the list, and I may take it they will also be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I will just add that, as it concerns to the Official Note for Mr. Mladen Markac, that the Chamber already took the position as regards to Official Note for Mr. Cermak. So it is the very same procedural situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, the special position was, of course, raised by Mr. Cayley very specifically as far as Mr. Cermak is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Well, I had not to be repeated if I just accept, on the same basis, all the reasons that Mr. Cayley has stated, that these are the very same that the Markac state as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Without having it reviewed again, the Chamber will give a decision soon, but perhaps not today. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: May I call document 1241, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And while that document is brought up, Mr. Zganjer, if could I take you to paragraph 10 of your supplementary statement. At line 4, you start off by saying: "I'm not aware of any police or other investigation which was carried out into this incident," and you're referring to the Grubori incident which you have referred to in line 3, "prior to the investigation I initiated ..." --

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO ZGANJER
utterances.text: I apologise. What paragraph is that?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... paragraph number 10 of your supplementary statement. Do you have it?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO ZGANJER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: You refer to the Grubori investigation and you go on to say: "I'm not aware of any police or other investigation which was carried out into this incident prior to the investigation I initiated in 2001. If the police had instigated an investigation, the investigating judge would have been informed. In March/April 1998 following territorial reorganisation, Knin came under the jurisdiction of Sibenik-Knin county court." This is what you just stated a little while ago, too. "Sometime after that, I began to receive information from Amnesty International and Croatian Helsinki Committee concerning the events in Grubori. I then contacted the police to ascertain what information existed concerning this matter. Prior to 1998, the Zadar county court had jurisdiction to initiate an investigation into Grubori. Mr. Galovic, the Zadar state county [sic], confirmed to me that they had not received any report from the police regarding the incident; and, as such, there had been no investigation initiated by the Zadar county state attorney. I personally believe that this matter should have been reported to the state attorney and investigative judge on duty at the time of incident." Now, I appreciate you may not have seen the document which is on the screen right now. That is a memo sent to the county public prosecutor. It was a memo sent to the public prosecutor of the Republic of Croatia by county public prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And if we could go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Is that the person you mentioned as your colleague in Zadar county court?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO ZGANJER
utterances.text: You mean the county attorney's office in Zadar? Yes. Ivan Galovic is his name. You're showing me a document bearing the date 18 December 2003, if I'm not mistaken. This is letter sent by the county attorney's office in Zadar. This letter bears a stamp, and it was signed by Mr. Ivan Galovic, the state attorney in Zadar.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And, Mr. Registrar, if we could just go to page 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: There in paragraph 1 he reports to the state attorney of the Republic of Croatia that: "We have not received a criminal report or a standard," that is could be a translation issue there, "report regarding killings in the hamlet of Grubori." Then the next paragraph reads: "2 and 4, regarding killings in the hamlet of Gosic and village of Varivode of seven persons with the last name Borak in Gosic and seven persons with the last name Beric, Dusan Djukic, and another person in Varivode, we filed an indictment against Pero Perkovic et al for crimes under Article 34, paragraph 2 of the KZRH Criminal Code of Republic of Croatia."

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And if you could move to next page.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Right at the top, it says: "The county court in Zadar acquitted the accused of the said crimes which were described in the first instance judgement under items 4 and 7. "The Supreme Court of the Republic of Croatia upheld the appeal of the public prosecutor, and on the grounds of erroneously established facts, quashed the judgement pertaining to the said crimes. "The case was then remitted to the competence of the county public prosecutor's office in Sibenik on 4 October 1999." That is correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO ZGANJER
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. Let's go back to item number 1, please. It is true, and it is confirmed by Mr. Ivan Galovic in this letter, that they never received a criminal report or any other report for the killings in Grubori. I'm referring you to the part of my statement in which I said that, in a telephone conversation, I had learned that myself from Mr. Galovic. That was sometime towards the end of 1998 or beginning of 1999. I can't pinpoint it exactly the time of that telephone conversation. In that telephone conversation, he confirmed to me what he states in this letter dated 18 December 2003. I would like to add that items 2 and 4 also reflect the truth; that is, items 2 and 4 in this letter. After it was quashed by the Supreme Court of the Republic of Croatia, the case was then remitted to the competence of the county public prosecutor's office in Sibenik and the county court in Sibenik, and we're talking about a case --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zganjer.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, can this document be entered into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I hear of no objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit number P1061.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I note the time, Mr. President, and I apologise for the five minutes I have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I didn't want to interrupt the witness in giving his last answer. Ms. Mahindaratne, could you tell how much time you would still need.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I believe about 30 to 40 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zganjer, we'd like to see you back tomorrow when the examination will continue. I instruct you that should not speak with anyone about the testimony you have given until now or the testimony still to be given tomorrow. You should refrain from any conversation with whomever on that subject. As far as resuming tomorrow is concerned, unfortunately, the Presiding Judge is not available and up until 10.00, and my consultation with the other Judges was just about to learn whether they would continue under Rule 15 bis. They decided that they will not, which means we will resume tomorrow at 10.00. Tomorrow, Tuesday, 11th November, at 10.00, Courtroom I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 11th day of November, 2008, at 10.00 a.m. 25
